Replay

Create/join protocol and Godot connection

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Server ownershipWire and retry contractGodot connection and TLSRemaining integration

Use this protocol to create rooms and issue, consume or revoke invitations through the admission backend. It provides canonical request/reply messages, a bounded room hub and a Godot client connection requiring verified TLS by default. Native tests create rooms, issue/use invites, authenticate authority RPCs, reconnect, and recover the same credentials after a server kill/restart. The recorded gate separates this local TLS acceptance from public deployment and browser enrollment.

Server ownership#

Hub_Config selects one game content ID, the policy for new rooms, and a resident room limit (1–32, default 16). hub_open receives the complete existing bundle set before accepting traffic. sqlite.load_all reads that inventory transactionally into a caller-bounded destination; excessive, corrupt or wrong-content rows fail without returning a partial inventory. One service owns this room set. Multiple instances sharing the database reject stale writes from one another. This does not provide a highly available coordinator cluster.

New cooperative rooms use a client-supplied nonzero room ID and fresh 32-byte creator claim. Retain both before sending. A collision with another creator's room fails the claim check. Retrying a successful create with the same room, claim and endpoint returns the same credential; changed endpoints fail. Content and policy come from server configuration, not client permission fields. Existing rooms retain their persisted policy after restart.

Public creation in a dedicated deployment is denied: its bootstrap credential belongs to infrastructure. Trusted deployment code must construct and persist such rooms before public admission starts. Ordinary-player invites remain available; trusted-player invites remain denied. A previously provisioned dedicated creator claim is an explicit infrastructure capability.

Creation persists before publishing a room or grant. An uncertain create commit stops the whole hub from serving until startup reloads its inventory. An uncertain join follows the room owner's existing fail-closed rule. Unknown-room requests neither load storage nor trigger coordinator generation changes.

Poll the transport once per update and bound its ingress loop. Pass provisioning packets to hub_receive and authority RPCs to hub_control_receive. Both can share a connection; authority still checks its MAC, nonce/incarnation, request frontier, lease and own budget. hub_room exposes a room to trusted embedding code. RTC rendezvous can bind to that room's service; multi-room signaling routing and game frontends still need integration.

Admission has a global burst/rate of 32 requests and 32 requests/sec, and per connection a burst of 8 and 4 requests/sec. It retains at most 128 peer budget entries, reusing entries after 10 seconds of inactivity. The transport must also bound handshakes, connections, ingress and buffers. These limits do not replace account authorization, per-user creation quotas or room retirement. Rooms remain resident for the hub's lifetime and persist across restarts.

Wire and retry contract#

The optional human-entered short room code v1 is a client-side recipe using this existing protocol. short_code maps a random creator claim and content ID to five characters from ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789. Separate HMAC-SHA256 domains derive the room locator and two invitation secrets (crew index 0, watch index 1). creator_short_invite registers only .Player, one-use invitations; the normal server authorization checks still require the full creator claim. Codes are case-insensitive and trimmed at the edges. Other input is rejected. The independent member/creator credentials, message shapes, protocol version, stored bundle schema, request budgets and long RP1 ticket format are unchanged.

Protocol version 1 uses canonical envelopes: request kind 0x5051, reply kind 0x5053, epoch 1, tick zero and the configured content ID. Fixed-size messages fit within PACKET_BYTES (1024). Wrong schema/version/content, noncanonical fields, invalid enums and wrong sizes are rejected before admission mutation.

Request Required fields beyond room/content/version/verb
Create claim: creator secret; endpoint: advertised gameplay endpoint
Invite claim: creator secret; ticket: new invite secret; role; uses
Join claim: guest's fresh retry secret; ticket: invite secret; endpoint
Revoke claim: creator secret; ticket: invite secret

Unused fields must be zero. Replies contain the SHA-256 hash of the exact request and matching room/content, plus a grant, ticket or error with empty result values. Clients reject unrelated or malformed replies. Retrying the same committed request through a new client or transport connection returns its saved result.

The generic Client borrows a transport and clock. It keeps one request pending, retries identical bytes every 250 ms, and returns Not_Ready after 10 seconds without a correlated reply. Timeout is an uncertain outcome, not proof of failure; retry the same persisted request. Clock failure/reversal is explicit. client.complete and client.reply expose completion. Closing clears owned protocol buffers/credentials but does not close the borrowed transport.

This protocol is not encryption. The embedding must provide authenticated, confidential transport or an explicitly local test channel. Claims and credentials are bearer capabilities. Never put them in URLs, logs, gameplay snapshots or authority backup archives.

Godot connection and TLS#

replay/godot.Provision_Connection owns the socket and protocol client:

Odin
connection: rgd.Provision_Connection
err := rgd.provision_connect(&connection, "wss://rooms.example.test/admission")
// Persist room_id and creator_claim before submission. Check every error.
err = rgd.provision_request(&connection, {
    version = provision.PROTOCOL, verb = .Create,
    room = room_id, content = content_id,
    claim = creator_claim, endpoint = advertised_endpoint,
})
err = rgd.provision_frame(&connection) // call from _process until complete
// Consume connection.client.reply only when connection.client.complete is true.
// Persist a successful grant before treating enrollment as recoverable.
rgd.provision_disconnect(&connection)

The URL must use wss://. Explicit local_development=true permits only literal localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] with a valid port. Userinfo, misleading suffixes and non-loopback WS endpoints are rejected. Godot validates remaining URL syntax. The wrapper reconnects dropped sockets at most every 500 ms, retaining its request.

Optional native TLSOptions.client can supply a private CA. Unsafe client and server options are refused on client connections. Browsers use their trust store; WASM compilation does not prove browser TLS enrollment. The test fixture installs no trusted root on the host machine.

websocket_host(..., tls=server_options) retains server TLS options and wraps accepted TCP streams. Handshakes occupy bounded slots and must complete within the configured deadline before HTTP/WebSocket acceptance. Closing releases open peers and pending TLS streams. Existing plain WebSocket callers retain their behavior. Godot documents these underlying TLS stream and WebSocket acceptance APIs; fixtures verify the adapter under Godot 4.7.1.

room_with_grant(options, grant) validates content/credential shape and copies room, identity, key and stable game token into Room_Options. It keeps challenged process registration, clearing provisioned_incarnation and the session incarnation hint. Creator member 1 is bootstrap. Connection settings/model configuration remain game inputs. Membership and hosting permission do not confer a live authority lease.

Remaining integration#

The client enrollment journal persists pending requests before submission and successful credentials before use, with native SQLite and browser IndexedDB acceptance. The older TLS fixture still uses predetermined test claims and fingerprints; the enrollment fixture generates fresh claims and exercises the actual journal. The room service and the Cavecrawl/Scrapyard party menus integrate it with per-room RTC signaling and a reproducible co-op invite. Other game menus, general invite-operation persistence, public TLS/relay deployment and account/room lifecycle remain work. Original games and their existing fixture provisioning remain separately runnable.
